newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1-dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt higher amid support from light hog marketings, livestock dealers said.
Marketings this week were curtailed by a seasonal reduction in hog supplies, the dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant were seen steady at $58.00.

The top plant hog price Wednesday at $58.00 reflected a recovery of $2.00 from the $3.00 that were lost when hogs held back by the Memorial Day holiday weekend flooded the market last week, the dealers said.
Illinois top prices for hogs delivered to the plant could range $58.00 to $58.50, they said. Indiana/Ohio top hog prices at the plant were seen at $58.00.
Gains were seen furthered by outlooks for continued pork strength, the dealers said.
Central U.S. carlot pork prices were quoted midday $2.00 to $3.00 higher for loins, $1.00 to $2.00 higher for hams and $1.00 to $2.00 higher for pork bellies, USDA reported.
Pork price strength was tied to light offerings following last week's holiday-shortened slaughter, the dealers said.
